question: Which of the following is/are NOT present in the plasma?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Undigested food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plasma** is the liquid component of blood that holds the blood cells in whole blood in suspension.
 
• It is composed mainly of **water** (about 90-92%) and contains various substances including **salts, proteins, hormones, and waste products.**
 
• **Salts** in plasma help in maintaining osmotic balance, pH, and various other functions crucial for homeostasis.
 
• **Proteins** in plasma include albumins, globulins, and fibrinogen, which play essential roles in maintaining osmotic balance, immune response, and blood clotting.
 
• **Hormones** are also found in plasma and are vital for regulating physiological activities and maintaining homeostasis.
 
• However, **undigested food** is not present in the plasma as it is usually processed and absorbed in the digestive system, and only nutrients absorbed from the food enter the bloodstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Salts**__

 __
 
• Salts such as sodium, potassium, calcium, and magnesium are crucial for various **cellular functions** including nerve transmission and muscle contraction.
 
• They help to maintain the **osmotic balance** and pH levels in the blood.
 
 
 
• **Proteins**__
 __
 
• Proteins in plasma serve multiple functions including transport, immune defense, and **blood clotting**.
 
• Albumins maintain **osmotic pressure**, globulins are involved in the immune response, and fibrinogen is essential for the **clotting process**.
 
 
 
• **Hormones**__
 
 
• Hormones are chemical messengers that regulate **physiological processes** including growth, metabolism, and reproductive functions.
 
• They are secreted by various **endocrine glands** and transported via plasma to target organs.
